issues.description: Aufgabe 10 (problem_statement.md) requires: "die Anzahl von Wanderwegen, die zu einer Gemeinde führen" (Ausgabe: Gemeindeschluessel und Anzahl, absteigend nach Anzahl). The solution file solution_repository/aufgabe10.sql instead counts rows from the Gemeinde table (SELECT gemeindeschluessel, COUNT(*) AS Anzahl FROM Gemeinde ...), which counts Gemeinde rows per key (typically 1) rather than counting Wanderwege that lead to each Gemeinde. This is a semantic/structural mismatch between the problem requirement and the provided solution and will produce incorrect results and confuse students about which table/relationship to aggregate.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the solution query to count Wanderweg rows (or the mapping rows linking Wanderwege to Gemeinden) grouped by gemeindeschluessel instead of counting rows in Gemeinde. For example, if Wanderweg has a foreign key to Gemeinde: SELECT g.gemeindeschluessel, COUNT(w.wanderweg_id) AS Anzahl FROM Wanderweg w JOIN Gemeinde g ON w.gemeindeschluessel = g.gemeindeschluessel GROUP BY g.gemeindeschluessel ORDER BY Anzahl DESC; Or, if there is a join/mapping table (e.g. Wanderweg_Gemeinde), count that table: SELECT wg.gemeindeschluessel, COUNT(*) AS Anzahl FROM Wanderweg_Gemeinde wg GROUP BY wg.gemeindeschluessel ORDER BY Anzahl DESC. Verify the schema for the exact table/column names and update the solution (and template example) accordingly so the aggregation matches the task description.
